node_definition.done_when: Read section 33 of crew-runtime-positive-controls first. Establish the order of the steps in complete() in reckon/crew/promotion.py: which steps release the workspace, remove the live pointer or write the ledger, and which refusals come after any of them. State that order in the evidence fragment, with function names and line numbers from the committed blob. Then reorder so that every refusal is reached before any workspace, pointer or ledger side effect, and a refused promotion leaves the worktree, the live pointer and the ledger exactly as they were. tests/test_refused_promotion_leaves_the_worktree.py drives a promotion refused on an accept-path claim conflict (a second live pointer claiming the accepted path), in a temporary git repository and RECKON_HOME. It asserts afterwards that the worktree directory still exists, the live pointer is unchanged, and no ledger row was written. A second case drives one other refusal that, at the base revision, is reached after a side effect, if the order you establish shows one. Existing tests that call complete() keep passing; grep tests/ for crew complete and for the complete function to build the gate, keeping it to the files that reach the steps you move. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/refused-promotion-leaves-the-worktree.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
